Coupled with changing customer delivery and installation schedules, new orders are delayed and revenues are shifted into 2027 despite our significant order backlog.

In Peru, an agreement originally expected to be signed at the first half of 2026 was signed at the end of the third quarter, shifting the associated revenues into 2027. In contrast, our Defense business continues to gain momentum and to deliver strong revenue growth, exceeding our expectations. In light of these dynamics, we are updating our full year guidance. We now expect revenues in the range of $455 million to $475 million. The impact on adjusted EBITDA is much more modest, thanks to cost-saving initiatives we have implemented and a favorable revenue mix. As such, we are narrowing our adjusted EBITDA guidance to between $61 million to $63 million.

A few years ago, we anticipated the change is now occurring in the Commercial market. We have been aggressively preparing by shifting our focus and investment to Defense, beginning with the acquisition of DataPath in 2023. We are building on this strategy with pending acquisition of Comtech Satellite and Space business, which we expect will significantly expand our Defense business, strengthen our position in the U.S. market and broaden our technology portfolio. We expect Comtech to add more than $180 million in revenues and more than $80 million in adjusted EBITDA.

The closing of the transaction is still subject to remaining U.S. regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, which we expect to receive before the end of the year with closing targeted right after. Now on to the business review. I will start with the Defense. During the third quarter, Gilat Defense strengthened its market position, driven by increasing demand for multi-band mobile, rapidly deployable SATCOM solutions that give users resilience and greater flexibility in scaling the relocating network assets to achieve operational continuity on the battlefield. Specifically, Gilat DataPath received an award of more than $32 million for multi-band DKET systems supporting U.S. Defense network resilience.

We are also advancing our DKET multi-orbit capabilities to give Defense customers greater operational flexibility. Gilat DataPath is advancing DKET certification for its transportable gateway systems for operation of both the U.S. Department of War, WGS Network and SES' Empire Sovereign Network. This builds on existing technology and creates an additional growth opportunity for Gilat Defense. We also announced additional orders of more than $8 million from the U.S. Department of War for field services and SATCOM solution upgrades. During the quarter, we achieved an important technology milestone by successfully demonstrating an AI-based capability that detects and cancels interference on satellite links. This innovation supports reliable communication in increasingly complex satellite environments and reflects our ongoing investment in advanced technologies.

Overall, our Defense business continues to build momentum. These awards deepen our relationship with the U.S. Department of War and reinforce our position as a trusted provider of advanced SATCOM solutions for complex operational environment. Turning to Commercial. Our performance reflects both competitive pressure in traditional markets such as enterprise and cellular backhaul and delays in customer programs as discussed earlier. During the quarter, we received more than $10 million in additional SkyEdge IV orders from a leading satellite operator. During the third quarter, we delivered more than 150 Sidewinder ESA terminals.

In parallel, we have entered into ongoing negotiations with key customers to secure more favorable revenue -- sorry, more favorable economic terms for Gilat, and we expect this delay to delay some orders and revenues to 2027 and beyond. At the same time, our customers continue to add new airline to their backlog, and we expect additional orders in line with their installation needs in 2027 and beyond. Longer term, we are also making good progress certifying our multi-orbit Sidewinder ESA terminal as a line-fit solution with Boeing and Airbus. This program is expected to expand our margins and strengthen the profitability of the Sidewinder business over time with delivery of the first units expected before year-end.

We are also investing in our integrated solutions and digital inclusion offering, which integrates connectivity, complementary technologies and platforms to deliver end-to-end essential digital inclusion programs. We are advancing in several large opportunities, and we are very optimistic about the potential this represents for Gilat. Lastly, we also see opportunities developing with several large HTS and VHTS satellite expected to launch in late 2027 and onwards. Our Peru business continued to build on its extensive experience deploying, upgrading and operating large-scale integrated solutions and telecommunication networks throughout the country. During the quarter, we announced 2 significant projects. First, we signed a $28 million contract with Pronatel to upgrade the broadband network in the Ica region.

Ica represents the fifth regional broadband network upgrade awarded to Gilat since 2025. We also signed a $14 million agreement for digital inclusion project. The project will extend broadband access to schools, health care facilities and other public institutions in underserved communities, improving access to essential services. The experience provides a strong foundation for pursuing additional opportunities in Peru and elsewhere in the region as governments invest in connectivity and digital development. During the quarter, we announced a private placement of $100 million in 5-year convertible notes. The financing give us additional flexibility to pursue organic and inorganic opportunities, particularly in Defense and Space, while funding the technologies and capabilities needed to support our ambitions in these markets.

Gilat is navigating changes in the commercial satellite market while transforming its business mix and focus, expanding its Defense operations and placing greater emphasis on growth and profitability. In closing, the third quarter reflects both opportunities and challenges in our evolving markets. Competitive pressure, longer decision-making process and GEO and LEO launch delays, customer delivery changes and ongoing commercial negotiations have shifted revenue timing and have affected our revenue outlook. We are actively addressing these challenges while making clear progress on our long-term strategy. Our Defense business is growing with a 53% increase year-over-year in revenues. Our profitability continues to improve, and we are investing in technologies and capabilities that we believe will support our future growth.

The Comtech acquisition represents a major step in our transformation, adding meaningful scale to the business and further strengthening our position in the U.S. Defense and Space markets. At the same time, we remain focused on capturing opportunities in next-generation ground infrastructure, IFC, new HTS, VHTS and NGSO satellite constellations and integrated connectivity solutions. We recognize the importance of delivering on our commitments and providing greater visibility as this initiative progress. Our priority remains clear: to build a stronger, more diversified and more profitable Gilat positioned for sustainable long-term growth. And with that, I will hand over the call over to Gil Benyamini, our CFO. Gil, please go ahead.

Gil Benyamini: Thank you, Adi. Good morning and good afternoon to everyone. I would like to remind that our financial results are presented both on a GAAP and non-GAAP basis. I will now walk through our financial highlights for the third quarter of 2026. Our third quarter results demonstrate the continued transformation of our business mix, strong growth in Defense, higher gross margins and disciplined cost management drove 13% increase in adjusted EBITDA and approximately 2% of margin expansion despite slightly lower revenue. In terms of our financial results, revenue for the third quarter were $116.2 million, representing 1% decrease compared with $117.7 million in Q3 '25.

The revenues for the Commercial segment in Q3 '26 were $69.7 million compared with $73 million in the same quarter last year. 4% decline year-over-year was primarily driven by lower amplifiers deliveries to certain customers that were deferred to later periods. Revenues for the Defense segment in the third quarter of 2026 were $36.9 million, 53% higher than $24.1 million in the same quarter last year, primarily driven by transportable product deliveries at Gilat DataPath. Q3 '26 revenues for the Peru segment were $9.6 million, 54% lower than $20.6 million in Q3 '25. The decrease mainly reflects lower construction revenues from the upgrade projects, as well as hardware-related delivery revenues recognized in the same quarter last year.

Our GAAP gross margin in Q3 '26 was 35% compared with 30% in the same quarter last year. The increase compared to Q3 '25 is mainly attributed to a more favorable deal mix in the Defense segment as well as improved profitability in Peru. GAAP operating expenses in Q3 '26 were $32.9 million compared with $27.2 million in Q3 '25. The increase was primarily attributable to changes in the U.S. dollar versus Israeli shekel exchange rate, Comtech Satellite and Space transaction-related expenses and a provision for bad debt due to 2 customers entering into Chapter 11 in the U.S. As a result, GAAP operating income was $7.9 million compared to $7.5 million in Q3 '25.

GAAP net income in Q3 '26 was $8.7 million or a diluted income per share of $0.11 compared with GAAP net income of $8.1 million or diluted income per share of $0.14 in Q3 '25. The increase in net income was primarily driven by the higher operating income, while diluted income per share declined due to the higher share count mainly related to equity raises that we did. Turning to non-GAAP results. Our non-GAAP gross margin in Q3 '26 was 36% compared with 32% in Q3 '25. The increase is primarily attributable to the Defense and Peru segment. Non-GAAP operating expenses for the quarter were $27 million compared with $24.7 million in Q3 '25.

The increase mainly reflects the impact of the U.S. dollar versus the Israeli shekel and approximately $1.3 million of bad debt expenses, partially offset by lower R&D expenses, which decreased mainly due to higher R&D grants and NRE expenses related to revenue-generating projects reclassified to cost of revenue. Non-GAAP operating income in Q3 '26 was $14.6 million, 14% higher than the $12.8 million in Q3 '25. Non-GAAP net income in Q3 '26 was $14.3 million or a diluted income per share of $0.18 compared with a non-GAAP net income of $11.8 million or income per share of $0.19 in Q3 '25.

Adjusted EBITDA reached $17.6 million, 13% higher than Q3 '25 despite lower revenues, reflecting a favorable business mix and our cost efficiency initiatives. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to approximately 15% compared with approximately 13% in Q3 '25. For the first 9 months of '26, adjusted EBITDA was $48.1 million, 37% higher than the same period last year on revenue growth of 11%. Moving to the balance sheet and cash flow. During the quarter, we generated approximately $4.3 million in operating cash, mainly reflecting significant collections from customers in the Commercial and Defense segment, partially offset by working capital buildup related to revenue recognized in Defense with collection expected in subsequent periods.

During the quarter, we also completed the issuance of $100 million 5-year convertible notes with net proceeds of approximately $99 million. We ended the quarter with a strong liquidity position of $260 million comprised of cash, cash equivalents and short-term deposits. Net of the convertible notes and short-term loan, our net cash position was $158 million compared with $157 million at the end of the second quarter this year. DSO were 111 days, excluding Peru construction activity and remained within our expected range. Our shareholders' equity as of September 30, '26 totaled $555 million compared with $545 million on June 30, '26.

Looking ahead, based on our third quarter results, backlog and current visibility, we're updating our full year '26 guidance. Revenues are now expected to be between $455 million and $475 million, representing 3% growth year-over-year at the midpoint compared with our previous range of $500 million to $520 million. The update mainly reflects lower order intake expected in Q4, resulting from delays in GEO and LEO launches, rescheduled IFC deliveries and timing of Peru agreements, which shifted revenues into 2027 in future periods. We're narrowing our adjusted EBITDA guidance to between $61 million and $63 million, representing 17% growth at the midpoint.

The impact on adjusted EBITDA is considerably more limited than our revenues, supported by favorable deal mix and the cost-saving initiatives we've implemented. This outlook continues to absorb the impact of the unfavorable movements in Israeli shekel versus the U.S. dollar on our operating expenses. The updated outlook does not include any contributions from pending Comtech Satellite and Space acquisition. That concludes my financial review. We would now like to open the call for questions. Operator, please go ahead.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] The first question is from Ryan Koontz of Needham & Company.

Ryan Koontz: I want to ask about the Commercial pushouts here, maybe starting with IFC. Is this related to new versions that are lower cost rolling out? Or you're trying to secure some pricing adjustments? Or can you give me some context of kind of what's driving the pushouts from your IFC customers?

Adi Sfadia: Sure, Ryan. So generally speaking, we see some installation delays that shifted some of the deliveries to 2027. In parallel, as we said in the last several meetings, the profitability on the retrofit units are limited and close to breakeven. We would like to ensure that we will make profits on the retrofit as well. Line-fit will be profitable units, but we would like to make sure that we'll make profits on the retrofit as well. So we are working in 2 fronts. One is a cost reduction initiative that takes much longer time than originally anticipated. And in parallel, we started negotiation with customers to have better economics on the unit price.

Ryan Koontz: Yes. That makes sense. Was there something that changed from -- over the last few quarters? Or this is just continued kind of weak economics here that you thought -- you anticipated would get better over time? Is it...

Adi Sfadia: So we anticipated costing will get better over time, and it take much longer time than expected. We had a tight delivery schedule with our customers that we wanted to make sure that they won't lose business. So we fought hard to deliver what they need on time. And in parallel, recently, we started a negotiation on the new contract terms, which we expect to delay some orders and will push some of the deliveries into 2027 onwards.

Ryan Koontz: Got it. And the Q3 deliveries, were those close to what you expected in terms of volume?

Adi Sfadia: Q3 deliveries are exactly as we expected at the beginning of the quarter and based on our plan. The miss on the Commercial this quarter was mainly related to large LEO project that we are delivering SSPA and because of the constellation rollout delays due to launch availability, the customer wants to push some of the deliveries onwards. We do have the units in inventory and backlog, and it's just a matter of time.

Ryan Koontz: Got it. Great. And the overall kind of upside in gross margin in the quarter here was a nice step-up. This is -- it sounds like it's from Defense mix mainly? Or what would you explain this nice step-up in gross margin in September?

Gil Benyamini: Ryan, it's Gil. So this would be a mix. Majority comes from the Defense section as the Defense is growing, and we saw a very nice growth of 53% in the Defense segment. We enjoy economy of scale, that was part of the upscale in the gross margin. And the second part comes from more profitable products that were delivered this quarter, mainly DataPath transportable products. So it's a mix of both. On top of that, we also gained a higher gross margin in the Peru division compared to last year and last quarter.

Ryan Koontz: Helpful. And maybe on the Defense side there, I know you had announced some collaboration with some optical transport space to ground technologies. Any update there you can provide on those new collaborations and products?

Adi Sfadia: So this is an initiative that we are working on almost 2 years. We had a proof-of-concept. We have units that are delivering what we aim to, and now we are engaged with customers for selling transaction. It will take time, but it's something that we believe can drive DataPath and Gilat Defense future growth.

Ryan Koontz: Great. That's nice to hear. And then maybe on the Chapter 11 customer write-off, what was the time line here? I know the customer filed during the third quarter. Were these for recent shipments? Or was this debt that's been around for a while?

Adi Sfadia: It's -- that has been a while -- not for a while. It's relatively recent, but once the customer files for Chapter 11, we need to estimate what are the chances of collection, and we took a decision to write it off.

Operator: The next question is from Louie DiPalma of William Blair.

Louie Dipalma: You referenced the intensifying competitive pressure. For what end markets are you witnessing the biggest impact from the competitive pressure? Is it mostly specific to enterprise? Or are you also starting to see it on the aviation side? And is that the reason for some of the delays that took place? Because it seems that on the solid state power amplifier delays is more of a timing issue and not a competitive issue.

Adi Sfadia: Yes. So we feel the pressure on -- almost on all Commercial subsegments, especially on the enterprise and cellular backhaul. Over there, we feel a lot of pressure. And because there is a significant delays in GEO satellite launches, there is no -- relatively no new networks that are up for grab. So that's delayed orders. There are still several satellites that are expected to be launched in the second half of 2027 and 2028. So we do expect to see nice orders probably at the beginning of 2027 onwards. We do see also -- especially our customers see also competition on the aero side. But we know that our customers continue to win deals.

Their backlog is increased, and we do expect some large orders in the next few quarters. It's really tied to their installation schedule and the ongoing negotiation about better economics for Gilat in this sense. Now as we see today, also the aero is mainly a timing issue. We have significant backlog of units that we can deliver. And our customer has much more backlog than orders that they gave us. The Sidewinder terminal is their go-to-market on the Ku side, and we believe we'll get those orders. It's just a matter of reaching the right economic terms.

Louie Dipalma: Great. And is everything on track for the Comtech deal to close by the end of the year? And assuming that deal closes, what is the pro forma mix in terms of end markets for Defense versus Commercial versus Peru?

Adi Sfadia: Okay. So yes, first of all, the Comtech deal is on track. We received HSR blessing earlier the year. We are now in process of getting CFIUS approval. We expect to get it before the end of the year and closing will be right after. As for the mix, Gil will give you some greater data. But generally speaking, Comtech is going to add around $180 million of revenues. I would say 70% to 80% is Defense-oriented.

Gil Benyamini: In terms of percentage, so about 10% will be Peru and the rest 90%, each of the Commercial and Defense should be between 40% and 50%, depending on the final classification of all end markets.

Operator: The next question is from Sergey Glinyanov of Freedom Broker.

Sergey Glinyanov: I have a couple of them. What do you think about midterm election results and whether it may impact the Defense business? And if yes, what products are under the risk to your opinion?

Adi Sfadia: The midterm effect, it's a big question. It's -- first of all, it's really, it's early period. We don't really know what will happen, but we remain very confident in the outlook of the U.S. Defense business. Political changes can influence budget priorities and timing, but the need for resilience, secure mission-critical communication continues to increase. The acquisition of Comtech Satellite and Space Communication business will strengthen our position in the U.S. and it'll increase our product portfolio and we'll be in direct touch with the relevant Department of Defense entities together with Gilat existing capabilities. We believe it will continue to grow both on U.S. and globally.

So I think it's really early to say, but it's not changing our plans to invest in the U.S. The budgets in the U.S. are huge. It represents 70% to 80% of the overall satellite communication equipment market globally. And at the end, the overall U.S. budget will stay very big, and it depends on priorities within the budget. We believe that today, everyone understands that satellite gives you the resilience the battlefield needs.

Gil Benyamini: And I would like to add that it looks like most of the effect of the midterm should be affecting the reconciliation budgets and not the core budgets and our products are mainly targeted and acquired by the core budget. So as Adi said, we continue with our plans and hope that we'll see much higher revenues.

Sergey Glinyanov: Appreciate the answer. And also -- now more and more airlines are choosing Starlink as their primary IFC solution. So which is causing a lot of concerns about how demand will be affected across different providers and suppliers? How do you assess this kind of risk?

Adi Sfadia: First of all, it's true that Starlink is gaining market share. But as I said, our customers are also getting new deals and increasing their backlog. I think that the addition of line-fit for the Sidewinder increased the attractiveness of our customers. It's not a market that the winner take it all. I think that we are providing a unique terminal that allowed resiliency between LEO and GEO. There is no such antenna available today in the market. And if you -- we are the alternative for -- our customers are the alternative for Starlink.

And if you don't want to choose Starlink and you want GEO -- LEO resiliency, you need to go with -- at the end with Gilat equipment. And as I said, our customer has significant backlog, and we do expect large orders in 2027.

Sergey Glinyanov: Okay. And the last question relates to, is there any update on your Airbus line-fit?

Adi Sfadia: Yes. So we are progressing with both Boeing and Airbus line-fit. We expect Boeing certification to end before the end of the year and Airbus right after. We expect to deliver first unit to Boeing before the end of the year, and Airbus will follow.

Operator: The next question is from Chris Quilty of Quilty Space.

Christopher Quilty: I just want to start off with maybe a macro question on the antenna market, specifically the IFC antenna market and lots of changes there. What are you seeing in terms of technology trends, whether it's single orbit or multi-orbit, either frequency bands, Ku or Ka or a move from the sort of large LEO providers to some of the smaller constellations? Are there opportunities in the LEO market where a lot of them typically just bring the antenna with them?

Adi Sfadia: So, what we see today in the market, today, there is a Ka and Ku and you have the GEO-LEO play or the Starlink only LEO play. If you want GEO-LEO, you need to go with the Sidewinder terminal. What we see in the future based on discussion with players in the market is that the multi-orbit probably will stay. If it will be GEO-LEO or MEO-LEO, it's still under discussion. Definitely, terminals that will be able to connect both to Ku and to Ka on the LEO side will have better chances to succeed, and this is something that the direction that we are working on. We have started the initial development of such antenna.

This is what we are seeing in the market today. I believe that the Sidewinder still has a few hundreds, if not more than 1,000 units to be sold in the next 3 years.

Christopher Quilty: Got it. And switching gears, I mean, on the GEO satellite order side and launch situation, I haven't read the Airbus or Thales press releases, but did they announce further delays on the satellite delivery? Or is it looking more like launch delays?

Adi Sfadia: I think it's mainly connected to launch delays. You saw SpaceX announcement on Falcon 9. I think that Amazon is delaying a bit, Telesat is delaying a bit. So I think that the bottleneck right now is on the launch availability.

Christopher Quilty: Got you. And Gil, I guess, either a question or a request. I mean as the Comtech acquisition closes, if you can provide sort of the pro forma numbers there for us, that would be helpful as we do out the modeling for '27 and '28.

Gil Benyamini: Yes, sure. We will provide all the required data to the investors, and we're also anticipating to provide pro forma and Comtech acquired business on a solo basis as well. We'll do it after.

Christopher Quilty: Got you. Do you also intend at that time to provide update forecast both for the business and for '27?

Gil Benyamini: We'll do it together with Gilat guidance at the beginning of February '27.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] The next question is from Gunther Karger of Discovery Group.

Gunther Karger: I know that the expectation of closing the Comtech acquisition is by the end of the year. Is there anything specifically that's holding it up? Or is it basically on track?

Adi Sfadia: It's basically on track. Besides some customary closing condition, we are waiting for CFIUS approval. We already received CFIUS approval in 2023 for DataPath and in 2025 for Stellar Blu. So we don't see a problem with that. It's just a process that we believe will conclude before the end of the year.

Gunther Karger: But specifically, with regard to the government area, the CFIUS, is there any holdup there? Or is that basically also on track?

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. Mr. Benyamini, would you like to make a concluding statement?

Gil Benyamini: I want to thank you all for joining us to the call and for your time and attention. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter. Thank you very much, and have a great day.

Operator: Thank you. This concludes Gilat's third quarter 2026 results conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may go ahead and disconnect.

#3112. Google’s new AI tool just proved Signal encryption really works – here’s how

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With the aim of securing other vital systems, Google DeepMind plans to open-source its AlphaProof Code.

Researchers at Google DeepMind used AI to formally verify portions of Signal‘s underlying code — meaning they’ve mathematically proven that at least parts of the encrypted messaging app’s code do what they say, without errors. That’s reassuring given how many vulnerabilities AI systems have discovered in software lately, and how many people’s communications are protected by Signal’s cryptography. WhatsApp and Google Messages use the same encryption.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain

DeepMind used AlphaProof Code, “a novel agentic framework for formal verification at unprecedented depth that combines human expertise with AI agents,” the researchers said. They added that formal verification “is the highest standard of security assurance,” but, without automation at scale like AI systems, difficult and time-consuming.

AI companies like OpenAI have been on a math-breakthrough tear as of late, in some cases solving nearly century-old math problems with AI. By computing at such vast scale, AI models can rapidly accelerate much of the manual work mathematicians do.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

Using AlphaProof Code and building on earlier verification work by the Signal Foundation, DeepMind researchers divided the verification task into two camps. Humans worked with agents to identify what they needed to prove, and multiple agents running Gemini Carbon, the company’s latest model, then executed it. The agents also audited the proof and “highlighted areas that needed a second look by a human — just 1% of the codebase, a massive time savings,” the researchers wrote.

Also: After the vibe-coding rush comes the debugging hangover

For good measure, researchers tested AlphaProof Code’s ability to distinguish correct from flawed code by showing it two previously fixed Signal bugs, for which it produced correct proofs.

“Our work marks the first time AI has been used to formally verify a widely deployed cryptographic protocol at this depth,” the researchers wrote. “It’s also the first time the implementation of a widely deployed protocol like this has been formally verified by any method, with or without AI.”

Normally, researchers need to manually develop a proof to verify software, which takes much longer. That labor-intensive barrier has made formal verification a distant promised land, until now. The DeepMind team’s verification took a month to do what might normally take experts years.

DeepMind did not verify all of Signal’s code, but noted that this test is a step toward improved security infrastructure at a time when AI is disrupting the entire cybersecurity space.

Also: How to encrypt emails in Gmail, Outlook, and more

The breakthrough reiterates how deeply AI is both a massive risk for cybersecurity and an equally powerful fix. The year 2026 has been especially marked by AI-related security incidents, many of which involve agents. At the same time, companies like Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI are developing models geared specifically toward cybersecurity, including Anthropic’s Claude Mythos.

Also: How to easily encrypt your files on an Android phone

DeepMind did not share any plans to release its findings as a consumer product, though the researchers are open-sourcing their code to help others with formal verification efforts. “Verifying Signal’s core cryptography lays the groundwork to secure other vital systems, from medical device firmware to power grid software,” DeepMind added

Apple said the update fixes issues that could expose sensitive data.

Apple released iOS 27.2.1 on Monday, the same day the company released the first public beta for the upcoming iOS 27.3. The latest update fixes nine issues on your iPhone, including a couple that could expose your data to malicious actors.

You can download iOS 27.2.1 now by going to Settings > General > Software Update > Update Now and following the prompts on your screen.

Apple says the update provides bug fixes and security updates for issues on your iPhone, two of which may lead to memory corruption on your device.

Memory corruption happens when a program on your device incorrectly reads, writes or frees up memory. This can cause the program to crash, or it could expose sensitive data to others.

You should update your iPhone as soon as possible. Apple didn’t say that these issues were being actively exploited. However, it’s important to keep the software on your device up to date so you’re better protected against potential security threats.

For more iOS news, here’s what features and bug fixes iOS 27.2 brought to your iPhone. You can also check out our iOS 27 cheat sheet for more.

#3110. All your Apple devices need to be patched ASAP – here’s why

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Security updates for iPhones, iPads, Macs, Apple Watches, and Vision Pro just rolled out.

On Tuesday, Apple released security patches for iOS, iPadOS, MacOS, WatchOS, and VisionOS, which address wireless security flaws in Bluetooth pairing, AirPlay, and Messages.

According to Apple’s security notes, vulnerabilities can allow attackers to establish a Bluetooth connection without user interaction, bypass AirPlay connection rate limits, and join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages. Around half of these flaws were found internally by Apple, while the others were submitted by researchers.

You should update your devices now, as several generations are affected across device categories. The following software versions include patches:

Apple’s security notes list a fix for Messages to prevent attackers from remotely joining an iMessage group chat and reading its messages. According to Apple, “an authorization issue was addressed with improved validation” to fix the issue.

There was likely a flaw in Apple’s iMessage authorization logic that allowed an unauthorized user to inject themselves into a group chat roster without permission from an existing member.

Also: Your iPhone can spot scams for you with iOS 27

Another issue in Messages could allow an authorized added member to access messages within a group chat that were sent before they joined. According to Apple, the code that caused this issue has been removed.

One security fix across devices and software versions addresses an issue where a malicious actor could establish a Bluetooth connection to your device without user interaction.

Apple was not specific about which kind of Bluetooth attack this fix addresses; however, it’s reminiscent of Bluetooth Low Energy Re-Pairing vulnerabilities found earlier this year by French researchers.

This study explains how bad actors can exploit vulnerabilities in Bluetooth Low Energy pairing logic to execute one-click or zero-click impersonation and man-in-the-middle attacks against unsuspecting devices, regardless of Bluetooth version or security level.

Also: Beware of Bluetooth sniffers: Your favorite gadgets could expose you

The study was published in January of this year, and the researchers reported initial findings to Apple, which “[appeared] to have hardened the re-pairing logic in MacOS/iOS 26,” according to the study. It’s possible that Apple internally found another vulnerability in the same Bluetooth pairing logic, given how many devices across Bluetooth versions are affected.

According to Apple, this issue was fixed with “improved checks,” likely meaning strengthened verification steps during pairing.

Another vulnerability pertains to AirPlay, allowing an attacker within Bluetooth range or on the same network to bypass the rate limit on AirPlay pairing code attempts. This issue also affects iOS, iPadOS, MacOS, VisionOS, and WatchOS.

This vulnerability is similar to the AirBorne attack method. This report, published in 2025 by Oligo, describes how zero-click remote code execution, user-interaction bypass, denial-of-service, man-in-the-middle, and other techniques can be used to take control of a device that supports AirPlay.

However, the current security issue is likely less serious or far-reaching and was discovered internally.

For this issue, when you pair a device with an AirPlay receiver, such as an Apple TV, AirPlay-enabled TV, or Mac, it will prompt you for a security PIN to verify your device. You can only input an incorrect PIN a certain number of times before you’re denied pairing for a period of time.

Also: The new Apple TV 4K is always listening for ‘Hey Siri’

A vulnerability in this defense mechanism can allow an attacker within Bluetooth range of, or on the same network as, your device to use a brute-force attack, bypassing the mechanism that limits the number of incorrect PIN attempts, and eventually gain access to your device. There are only so many PIN combinations.

According to Apple, “a logic issue was addressed with improved state management” to fix this problem.

#3108. I found a hidden Android tool that solves all my tiny text troubles

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android

When the print on your Android display is too small to read, and the pinch-to-zoom feature isn't working as expected, try this.

How many times have you been on your phone, wanted to read something (a piece of news, a website, etc.), only to find the text is too small and every effort to zoom in doesn’t work?

Also: 7 Android accessibility features that can make your life easier

This happens quite often when I’m viewing content in the Google News app — especially in the morning, when my eyes are still in “wake up” mode. It can be frustrating. And it’s not only text. Sometimes there’s an image I need to enlarge, but for whatever reason, pinch-to-zoom isn’t working on that particular screen.

Fortunately, there’s an option you can enable to ensure you can always zoom in on your Android device, no matter what’s on the screen. The option is found in Accessibility and is aptly called Magnification. With this feature enabled, you can quickly zoom in on the screen to enlarge any displayed content. It doesn’t matter what’s on the screen or what app is showing the image, page, or text — Magnification will magnify it.

This iteration of the feature has been available since Android 15. I found it by accident while poking around the Settings page. Since then, I’ve used it quite a bit, and it’s eased my morning frustration with reading news sites.

The Magnification feature is quite simple: once enabled, a magnifier shortcut appears on the screen. Tap that button, and whatever is on your screen will increase in size. It’s really that easy. One caveat: As long as the Magnification shortcut is enabled, the button remains on your screen. You can move the button up and down or to the left or right side of the display, but if you want the feature enabled, the button must remain.

The good news, however, is that the button does fade a bit, so it’s not glaring and in your face. You can still see it, but it gets just enough transparency that it doesn’t stand out all that much.

Also: Android is getting my favorite iOS tracking feature

Open Settings by dragging the Notification Shade down twice, then tapping the gear icon (or tapping Settings in the App Drawer). Where this is located depends on the Android version you’re using and your device. For example, on my Pixel 9 Pro, it’s in Settings > Accessibility > Magnification. On a RedMagic 12 Pro, it’s in Settings > Features > Accessibility. If you don’t find it right away, open Settings and search for Magnification.

Once you’ve found the Magnification option, tap the On/Off slider until it’s in the On position, and the Magnifier button will appear on your screen. Tap the button, and whatever is on the display will enlarge enough that you shouldn’t have any trouble reading it.

Here’s a little tip: After tapping the Magnification button, whatever’s been enlarged can be scrolled vertically, but not horizontally. Fortunately, there’s a way to ensure that you can read everything on the page.

Also: I use Google Magnifier to read tiny print without my glasses

Tap the gear icon at the bottom right of the display to open the options pop-up. On this page, tap the “Magnifier size” icon that’s second from the right. This enables a movable magnifier you can place where you need it (kind of like a traditional magnifying glass). You can also change the size of the movable magnifier (by tapping one of the other “Magnifier size” buttons) as well as the size of the text when magnified (by dragging the bottom slider).

Also: RedMagic 12 Pro is the fastest Android phone I’ve ever seen

This feature has alleviated the early-morning frustration of having to squint (even with my glasses on) to read certain news sites. Give it a try and see if it doesn’t make your Android life a bit clearer.

#3107. Google Introduces 3 More Top-Level Domain Names, Including .Eat and .Fly

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Prospective website owners can now register domains geared toward food, travel and local bands.

We’re trained to type .com almost on autopilot, but more top-level domains are coming. You’ll soon see websites ending in .eat, .fly and .here. It’s a new way for restaurants, travel agencies and other service providers to customize their online presence.

Google successfully filed these domain types with ICANN, the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers, back in 2012, but only released the new registry options to the public on Tuesday.

There’s always a concern that someone will steal a business’ domain name, a process known as cybersquatting. To prevent new top-level domains from being registered and ransomed at high prices, Google’s partnered registrars offered .eat, .fly and .here websites to registered trademark holders ahead of a wider rollout. This closed access period lasted from Sept. 1 to Nov. 9.

Google’s blog post about the new domains revealed several big businesses that have already secured new web addresses during the trademark holder selloff. Wingstop bought up wingstop.eat, while agriculture and food-tech company Clayton Farms secured the america.eat address. Caddy, Canary and Voltair are some of the businesses with new .fly domains.

The most interesting assortment of companies have tied down .here addresses. In its blog, Google describes .here domains as denoting businesses “where people get things done.” They utilize fairly common words that people might search for. Real-estate app Zillow owns rent.here and sell.here, while bloodtest.here is owned by SiPhox Health, a home blood-testing service.

A number of Google-partnered registrars are now accepting registrations for the three new domain types.

There’s currently a one-time early registration fee associated with registering the new domain names, though it is diminishing and will completely disappear on Nov. 17. After that, any currently unused .eat, .fly and .here names can be registered and maintained at a fixed annual rate, just like any other type of domain.

A representative for Google didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Jonathan Assia: First of all, I think generally, volatility is good for trading and for traders. It's where they find a lot of the opportunities. And over, I'd say, the last 5 years, we've seen, in many cases, retail investors that are able to capture the deep to buy the deep. Of course, post volatility, sometimes if customers lose money, that sort of creates a cooling off period. So that's why we always see heightened volatility and then lower volatility continue with heightened volatility. I think last week's significant shift in the markets means more trading activity and also more opportunities for customers to find stocks that were at significantly higher valuations before and enter it into the market.

So again, generally, I think volatility creates opportunity in the trading markets. And of course, it means some customers need to manage their risk and manage their portfolios more actively.

Operator: And our next question comes from the line of Dan Fannon from Jefferies.

Daniel Fannon: I wanted to ask about expenses. You mentioned AI helping potentially marketing spend being more efficient. So if you could talk a bit more specifically about 4Q expense trends. And then as we think about next year, what is a reasonable kind of level of growth for overall expenses as you think about investments and priorities into next year?

Jonathan Assia: Sure. I'll touch a bit about marketing and then Meron can continue on OpEx. I think what we're seeing within the marketing landscape within channels is a shift in channels. We are seeing cost per clicks, for example, in Google Search specifically actually becoming higher and a shift towards actually other channels in parallel to Google. So a lot more influencer social media, helping our Pro investors actually get tools to promote themselves.

I believe that using AI enables both us to create significantly more content and more tailored content, both regionally and on the different product lines of eToro and to provide tools to our Pro investors to also tell their stories externally and actually promote their stories externally on social media. So I think we are seeing both shift in channels and AI, enabling us to focus on channels that require more content and more tailored content over time. With that to the expenses side, I'll move to Meron.

Meron Shani: Sure. So thanks for the question with regards to the OpEx side. So first on Q4, as we noted, Q4 is going to be lower compared to Q3 by 5% and plus. And in general, about AI and how it's becoming effective on the cost base. So a few layers on this. One, AI will certainly enable us to scale the business without growth in any cost base. So that's on that front. It helps us really automate a lot of processes. It helps us really reduce a lot of manual work. So that's very healthy also for the organization. Second, it helps us really automate and really build on white coding or any of the new tools.

It really helps us build a lot of systems that we had to buy from externally. So that really is getting us a very good position in the overall cost base.

Jonathan Assia: I'll add an additional point on Tori, our AI agent and its road map. We're in the process of now launching a new version, which we call Tori Reloaded, which actually goes through the entire database of all of the dialogues with customer service and is able to actually capture significantly a wider range of questions, again, with the new models of Grok plus training it on all of the questions and the dialogues, both with account managers as well with customer service. We're seeing the agent actually advancing its capabilities to basically answer all of the customers' questions and on the road map also to help them on their portfolio management as well.

Operator: And our next question comes from the line of James Yaro from Goldman Sachs.

James Yaro: I was hoping you might be able to speak to the TAM for prediction markets outside of the U.S. today. In other words, which geographies permit that and where you're operating in that business? And then where you think you could expand your prediction markets offering over time?

Jonathan Assia: Sure. So we've launched prediction markets on Zengo, the noncustodial wallet on DeFi together with Polymarket earlier this year. We generally see I'd say -- I'd break down prediction markets into 4. There's DeFi U.S., there's DeFi globally, and then there's TradFi or the regulated activity in the U.S. that is the CFTC DCMDCO. Outside the U.S., I'd say it's still very much an evolving regulatory landscape. We are talking to the European regulators about prediction markets as well as starting first in Latin America and Asian selected markets. We do believe that, again, on financials, prediction markets will fall under financial regulation.

I think in countries where you have more specific regulation around sports betting, I think that probably is going to be more challenging in regions like U.K., Europe and others. So again, our view is sort of splitting prediction markets, both to DeFi, TradFi, and then sports versus financials, which have a different regulatory analysis.

Operator: And our next question comes from the line of Ed Engel from Compass Point.

Edward Engel: Are you able to provide any details regarding the size and structure of the recent LB acquisition? And then I guess, how do you think about M&A moving forward? Are you still looking for new deals today? Or could the M&A focusing slow down a little bit as you digest some of the recent activity?

Jonathan Assia: Sure. So first of all, I do believe we have right now after announcing 4 acquisitions this year, we are going to slow down a bit to adjust and integrate all of the different companies we've acquired. We've always looked at integrating teams. Again, we're looking at the deal in Argentina as becoming our base for Latin America. We believe we can grow the Latin America to $100 million revenues within the next 2 to 3 years together with the LB team with us. The core that we've bought is actually the licenses, the team, a certain amount of customers and revenues, but that's a relatively small amount versus the size of eToro.

Do you want to add anything regarding the size of the LB?

Meron Shani: Yes, it's not something that's going to be material on the balance sheet. It's going to be less than $20 million.

Operator: And our next question comes from the line of Craig Maurer from FT Partners.

Craig Maurer: What direction did crypto invested amount per trade go in September? And if you could also discuss the drivers of the higher crypto take rate?

Jonathan Assia: Sure. I'll let Meron answer that.

Meron Shani: Sure. So in terms of the take rate, when we see lower, call it, activities of customers, it really depends on the direction. When the direction is positive and crypto pricing is higher, we see better take rates that's in general. Specifically, we also had the crypto Nostro that provided us another almost 0.5% of an increase to the overall yield.

Craig Maurer: Okay. And the question on amount per trade in September on crypto?

Meron Shani: I think September, like as we saw between different months, it might be impacted by the amount of copy trading that goes into each of those trades. So that will probably differentiate between different periods. If there is any increased activity in copy, we will see a reduced invested amount per trade. The way that we are looking at is, obviously, we look at the entire invested amount. This is really what drives the business.

Operator: And our next question comes from the line of Brian Bedell from Deutsche Bank.

Brian Bedell: Maybe just back to the -- I think you mentioned, Yoni, earlier the receipt of the RIA license, obviously, the smart portfolio rollout. But can you talk about how you're using that RIA license in the U.S. for copy trading? To what extent are the Pro investors in the U.S. getting -- who are able to get compensated? And then if you can update us on the number of Pro investors out of that 6,000 are now U.S.-based?

Jonathan Assia: Sure. So smart -- the RIA license was used right now to launch the smart portfolios first. So the smart portfolios are managed by us and by our partners. CopyTrader is still limited in the U.S. to club members. We are in dialogues with regulators to see how potentially we can either use their RIA or structure incentives to the Pro investors in the U.S. It's still a small number versus the 6,000. We are looking to actually expand some of the Pro investors outside the U.S. to help them create smart portfolios in the U.S. as well using the RIA license.

So the RIA license enables us to actually manage investments on the platform and will enable us to actually launch also more products for managed investments using Tori, our AI agent.

Brian Bedell: Interesting. Great. And then maybe just, Meron, on the sales and marketing spending plans. I guess as you think about the expansion in the U.S. next year with TradeZero, is there a ratio of sales and marketing to net contribution that we should be thinking? I know it spiked in the last couple of quarters on the lower net contribution. But are you still trying to manage this down to like 25%? Or is that run rate -- should we be expecting a higher run rate in 2027 as you try to expand in the U.S.?

Jonathan Assia: Sure. So strategically, we've looked at the band of 20% to 25% as we said earlier this year. We've actually accelerated with a very successful first half. Right now we're adjusting it back towards the range of 25%. And strategically, next year, we'll look at roughly the same area of 25% out of net contribution.

Operator: And our next question comes from the line of Alex Markgraff from KBCM.

Alexander Markgraff: I wanted to ask about one of the 4 pillars as you've laid them out, Neo-banking. Just sort of curious, when you look across the globe and across operating markets, I would love to hear more on just sort of why eToro wins in Neo-banking. I mean, I think it's a competitive product, a lot of relevant competitors across certain geos. So just maybe expand on the product set and maybe what you need to build there to remain competitive. And then would be curious just to hear a bit more on the acquisition strategy with respect to Neo-bank products.

Jonathan Assia: Sure. So first and foremost, Neo-banking for us started both through an acquisition, but also to cater to the local needs of our customers in different regions. We have now over 2.5 million local currency accounts, which is basically a virtual bank account, a virtual [indiscernible], which enables our customers to deposit and withdraw basically with no fees in real time right now in Europe, U.K., in euro and pounds, in Australia right now, in Denmark and we're adding more and more currency.

So first and foremost, this significantly improves the economics of customers in the deposit and withdraw process versus, for example, a credit card, debit card or a PayPal that, in many cases, is used as customers open and fund their account initially. Second part is the card. The card, the Visa debit card right now is offered to customers in the club of eToro that are also now launching through the paid subscription of eToro. So we do believe that the Neo-banking and the capabilities of Neo-banking increase the subscription model in eToro as well.

And we're planning to expand the card right now with Europe and the U.K., both to have a global offering to our global audience and also extend the card program to more of the customers in eToro. Right now it was for the 15%, 20%, which are the club member. We are planning to expand that to more customers. I'll give an example of, again, the synergies between the card and the Neo-banking to the trading platform. Right now we've launched buying power on both crypto and stocks in selected markets, which means you can actually move your portfolio, let's say, $20,000 of Facebook and $20,000 of Bitcoin into the eToro platform, then you can basically ask for buying power.

So on those $40,000, you can actually get an additional $20,000 in cash and then you can spend that cash directly from your debit card in store. So that basically creates a unified approach for an investment super app. We were still very focused on our core business, which is trading and investing. But we believe there is significant synergies in actually capturing the entire universe of both savings or more of the passive wealth management part as well as the Neo-banking part. We're not yet looking at Neo-banking as a customer acquisition channel. We're looking at Neo-banking as a product that increased attachment rates and increases ARPU and retention of customers over time.

Operator: And our final question for today comes from the line of Charles Bendit from Rothschild & Company.

Charles John Bendit: I just wanted to ask about the U.S. road map post the TradeZero acquisition. First, could you remind us whether your double-digit U.S. share ambition refers to customers' assets or volumes and whether your thinking there has changed in any way? And second, just curious whether you plan to separate out any U.S.-specific KPIs going forward? And third, it sounded like U.S. marketing spend fits within your group S&M guidance at 25% of net contribution. Does that imply a moderation in spend for the existing ex-U.S. business?

Jonathan Assia: Sure. Can you reiterate just the first question on the double-digit percent?

Charles John Bendit: Sure. So could you remind us whether your double-digit U.S. share ambition refers to customers, assets or volumes and whether your thinking there has changed in any way?

Jonathan Assia: Sure. So again, we're looking at always all 3 parameters when we're looking at all of the different regions. Right now, with the TradeZero acquisition, as we complete the acquisition and integrate, we're looking at how to basically look at the combined KPIs and how to split from the U.S. So that is not something that we've yet published and we'll probably talk to the analysts as we're looking forward.

Regarding the 25% net contribution, as we've said in the past, we're always looking at how some of the more profitable regions are financing less profitable regions or how growth markets or more mature markets are actually financing new markets in eToro, and we'll continue to do that, including looking at the U.S. With, of course, the TradeZero acquisition, that means that we already are starting from a position of having a significant U.S. business focused more on the active trader segment right now. But post integration, we plan to have both the product suites for the retail mass consumer as well as the active trader.

And we believe that means basically, we have a significant stepping stone on which we can continue scaling up the U.S. business. Anything to add there, Meron?

Meron Shani: No, I think the question was also about the ambition. So I think you noted in the past that we want to be double-digit on U.S. on number of customers as a starting point and that's going to be the driver also for the future KPIs to follow.

Operator: Thank you. This does conclude the question-and-answer session. I'd like to hand the program back to Daniel for any further remarks.

Daniel Amir: Thank you very much, everyone, from Miami.

#3105. Need more AI in Creator Studio? Apple may charge you for it

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With its new $50 AI usage packes, Apple is the latest company to introduce paid model for AI access.

There are plenty of AI subscriptions out there, but Apple’s AI features are among the few still accessible by simply purchasing a device. Now, Apple is shifting its business model by offering a one-time $50 purchase option to grant server-based AI capacity in some apps, starting with Creator Studio apps.

Apple is introducing a one-time purchase option for AI Usage Packs via app updates to Creator Studio. If you want expanded access to AI features in Final Cut Pro, Pixelmator Pro, the iWork Suite, and Logic Pro, you’ll need to pay.

Also: ChatGPT Plus vs. Google AI Pro: Two $20 plans, very different perks

The $50 fee applies to extra usage blocks and kicks in when you exceed predetermined limits in these apps. Instead of a recurring fee, Apple is hoping the one-time fee for intelligence usage packs will help the company offset some of the cost of AI. Users can buy a pack for Logic Pro now, and the other apps are expected to get it soon.

“Usage Packs may offer the option to prepay for the use of certain AI-based Services and represent the amount you have paid in advance for use of the respective Services,” according to Apple.

Apple’s one-time payment breaks away from what most companies are doing. Most companies offering AI tools try to offset the steep cost of running large language models (LLMs) by charging users for paid subscriptions. For example, Samsung is rumored to be planning such a subscription for Galaxy AI usage, including access to features that are currently free.

Also: The best tablets of 2026: Lab-tested recommendations

The Creator Studio apps are the only ones getting the Usage Packs for now. The legal terms for intelligence Usage Packs explain that these packs would be available in “AI apps,” which include not only Final Cut Pro, Compressor, Logic Pro, MainStage, Pixelmator Pro, Motion, but also Pages, Keynote, Numbers, Freeform, and other apps.

You’re not required to purchase the Usage Packs to enjoy the core functionality of the apps in the Creator Studio. However, the fact that the Usage Packs are to be applied to popular apps like Pages and Freeform begs the question of whether Apple plans to put a paywall on features that are currently free.

Some of the features for which you may be required to purchase Usage Packs once you exceed your limits include the generation of images, shapes, presentations, and presenter notes, as well as some assistant features. Usage limits reset each month.

Also: Alexa Tablet 12 Pro review: Forget everything you knew about Amazon tablets

You can view your usage status for each of the applicable apps on your iPhone or iPad by tapping on More (or the button with three dots), then Intelligence Features, and Show Usage Status. On a Mac, it’s available by accessing Intelligence Features from the menu bar of the app you’re using, then clicking on Show Usage Status.

Intelligence usage packs expire after 12 months, but they roll over each month if left unused.

#3104. Half of New Games on Steam Are Now Made With AI. How Does This Reflect the Gaming Industry?

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Most of those games are unpopular, with 10 or fewer reviews from gamers.

Steam, the digital marketplace for PC games from game studio Valve, has hit a major milestone, sparking pushback from parts of the gaming community: Approximately 50% of new Steam games in October were made with the help of AI.

This underscores a growing trend in gaming, where more games are made with some form of AI assistance — specifically, generative AI, which developers have used to generate code, art assets, voice lines and more. Developers are adopting the technology in increasing numbers.

The numbers come from a Reddit user who goes by Ploz, and who used Steam’s publicly available data to see how many newly released games relied on AI in some capacity. This was possible because of Valve’s AI disclosure policy for newly released games, which requires developers to state whether they used AI in making their game. The disclosure is part of the storefront’s publicly accessible records, allowing anyone to view it.

A Valve representative did not respond to a request for comment.

The data is a snapshot of the tidal wave of AI-made games flooding storefronts, most prominently Steam. But crucially, Valve has chosen not to limit this flood, washing its hands of the problem and leaving gamers to fend for themselves in finding quality games. Developers had already been struggling to get their games noticed, and Valve’s limited curation seems completely unprepared for the firehose of AI-made games churned out on an increasing scale.

Valve implemented the AI disclosure policy in January 2024 to increase developer transparency. At the time, only 1.4% of newly released games used AI. This increased to 13.4% by the end of 2024, then to 24% by the end of 2025. It now sits at 49.9%.

There are some caveats. The AI disclosure is only required for games that use AI to create player-facing content, such as artwork, sound, character dialogue and localization. The 49.9% figure is specific to these types of games and doesn’t account for developers who use AI for behind-the-scenes tasks such as coding and bug fixes. A Google Cloud survey conducted in August 2025 showed that 87% of developers use AI for backend work, which doesn’t require disclosure on Steam.

So it’s likely that the number of games on Steam built with AI assistance is greater than 50%. Ploz notes that the only way users can avoid AI-generated games is to manually check for AI disclosures.

According to Ploz, the most common use of AI in game development is for artwork, which was mentioned in 63% of disclosures. Text and translations gobbled up 30%, while music (21%), code (16%) and voices (7%) rounded out the list. Many developers had more than one of those areas named in their disclosure, and about a quarter of developers said they were using AI for their Steam store pages and marketing.

About 3% of developers used AI directly as a game mechanic. One such example is a driving simulator called Teach My Little Sister How to Drive. Developers use AI in the game to interpret a player’s voice commands and generate the sister’s responses. To keep a playable demo of the game available to the public, the development team, Easy Fox, is paying $1,000 every day just to cover these AI operating costs — an expense so high that it was forced to take out a loan simply to keep the demo running.

For development, there are loads of options. The Unity 6 engine came out in October 2024 and includes AI code assistance, AI asset generation and third-party integration with Claude Code, Gemini and Grok. Anthropic’s Claude is a fairly popular option among smaller developers, since it supports the ability to vibe code whole games, with ChatGPT, Gemini and GitHub Copilot as other options.

Many of the games being released with the AI disclosure on Steam can be classified as slop — a derogatory term gamers have applied liberally to titles that heavily lean on generative AI for development and look derivative of other popular games. According to Ploz, most AI-enabled games are small: Around 47% of new games with fewer than 10 reviews have an AI disclosure. Among developers who released more than 10 games in a year, 68% of those games included the disclosure.

Games with AI disclosures received fewer positive reviews on average than those without. And among all newly released games with more than 1,000 reviews, only 17% include an AI disclosure. That means gamers are still gravitating toward games without an AI disclosure and pushing back against games that use the technology.

Developers seem aware of this. CNET reached out to two dozen well-known developers, including Epic Games, EA, Activision Blizzard, Ubisoft, PlayStation Studios and many others. All of them declined to comment.

Bigger studios may be using AI in their development, but it’s hard to tell the scale. There’s no such thing as an AI audit yet, and the industry seems to be relying on voluntary disclosure for now. Steam’s disclosure policy has outed smaller developers who are either worried about violating the policy and being taken off the digital storefront, or aren’t worried about the negative effects of disclosure.

A lot of dominoes had to fall for this to happen. The availability of AI tools and the increasing ease of use are definite contributors. Subreddits like r/AIGameDev have plenty of examples of people putting together games with just a few days or weeks of vibe coding, which is a lot shorter than the standard video game development cycle, which can stretch over years depending on the scale, production level and graphics quality. This practice has exploded over the last couple of years, resulting in a lot of games getting launched that are made mostly or entirely with AI.

Many of these games end up on Steam, which doesn’t have a policy limiting AI-developed games.

“Digital storefronts like Steam have already struggled to moderate low-effort and poor-quality games, as well as copycats stealing other games’ ideas,” said CNET Managing Editor David Lumb.

Valve openly admits its role in this, stating that the problem definitely exists but that the company doesn’t “want to be gatekeepers telling developers which tools they should or shouldn’t use.”

It takes a similar stance on AI cloning, with Valve’s Tom Giardino telling developers that “you must continue to grow your game by adding features, personality and creativity that stem from your own perspective as a developer.”

These policies essentially allow any AI-developed game or clone to reach the Valve storefront without pushback, which certainly contributes to the flood of newly released games with some form of player-facing AI involvement in their development.

Rival store Epic Games has a similar stance, allowing basically any game that wants to be there. The company declined to comment further about this, but CEO Tom Sweeney is an avid supporter of AI in video game development, stating that it was “perfectly logical” for developers to rely on AI to handle the mundane grunt work that takes up most of a developer’s time.

While Steam and Epic Games tend to take a more lax attitude toward AI slop, other storefronts like Itch.io are not. Itch.io has a whole policy against AI slop and the company has willingly, and at times gleefully, deleted terabytes of AI slop from its storefront. It also requires developers to disclose if they used AI but takes a much more consumer-friendly approach by letting users filter those out of search results if they don’t want to see them.

Some measures are being taken to address the proliferation of AI slop, but none will entirely stop the problem. Cloning has been a problem for many years. Mobile gamers of a certain vintage may remember the flock of Flappy Bird clones that appeared on app stores after the original game went down, and those weren’t even made with AI.

AI makes cloning much easier and faster, and some AI companies are addressing it. Anthropic recently changed Claude Opus 5.5 to prevent it from generating copies of existing games. Anthropic engineering leader Addy Osmani posted on X that using Claude to copy games infringes on intellectual property rights and violates Anthropic’s policy.

However, during CNET’s testing, we found we could still make games resembling popular titles, so cloning remains possible with a little creativity.

“This has come up over and over on the subreddit r/GameDev, and there’s no real solution if Steam and other digital storefronts don’t stem the flood of low-quality AI games drowning out the labors of love that entertain and innovate,” Lumb said.

Many developers openly oppose AI and refuse to use it in their own work. However, as the Steam stats show, that crowd’s output appears to be getting smaller and smaller every year amid the unending stream of AI games.

#3103. The Austin Powers steamroller: How to trade CoreWeave's slow moving crisis

In Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery, a Virtuocon guard famously stands in front of a commandeered steamroller, screaming "No!!" three times before being run over. The joke, of course, is that the hazard moved so slowly he had ample time to step out of the way.

For months, equity traders holding CoreWeave (CRWV) have played that guard. Despite credit markets flashing warnings, equity holders essentially just stood there. Now, after a shocking 27.5% drop from last Friday's close to this Thursday morning's 52-week lows, followed by a whiplash 17% rebound, equity investors, if not squashed like Dr. Evil's henchman, are dazed and confused. Shares are down another 5% today.

With earnings just a few weeks away, massive leverage, a heavily split sell-side, and 15.4% short interest, the stock remains primed for explosive volatility.

The hazard approaching CRWV equity wasn't hidden. The AI cloud infrastructure platform essentially didn't exist five years ago and has accumulated $51.6 billion in debt (~$46 billion net of cash) against a backdrop of zero historical profitability. That was well known, but the CEO's comments that the company aspired to be investment grade so it could borrow "unlimited sums", even as investors already anticipated nearly another $60 billion in debt in the next 18months, spooked folks. (Trick or Treat!) Especially since the debt issued only in June had already fallen 20% since.

From an options trader's point of view, it was hard to reconcile deteriorating credit and rising leverage with falling options premia; as recently as last week, they were in the 6th percentile, 1.5 standard deviations below the one-year mean. At 72%, options weren't cheap in absolute terms, but given everything going on, they should have been higher. The stock also looked somewhat complacent, with the equity chopping around historical support levels dating back to May 2025. The credit side was on tilt:

Because CRWV is levered by more than 2:1, a 10% move in enterprise value translates to a nearly 22% swing in equity value.

Despite the dire credit picture, equity sentiment remains fiercely divided, driving this week's 17% bounce from the lows. For example, HSBC maintains a Sell rating with a $39 price target, essentially calling for the stock to be cut in half. Conversely, banks like BNP and Cantor Fitzgerald (my former employer) suggest these fears are overblown and the stock should more than double from here.

It's not just bankers defending the company either. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang downplayed systemic concerns, and ARK Investment stepped in to buy 192,000 shares. BofA argues that CRWV's ability to bring active power online at scale, combined with higher pricing from Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin deployments, will drive faster-than-expected revenue growth. They described execution risk as a bigger concern than financing; I'm not sure those who bought the 2032 8 1/2s at par would agree.

With CRWV's credit heavily distressed but its equity heavily defended by high-profile dip-buyers, going outright long or short into earnings carries excessive directional risk. A November/January Call Diagonal, currently trading for just under $6 per spread. Almost 9% of the current stock price. Normally, that's a lot, but given this stock has fallen 27.5% and then gained 17% in the past 5 sessions, it isn't.

#3102. New Windows 11 update fixes File Explorer menu mess – and patches an exploited flaw

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Windows > Windows 11

With the November Patch Tuesday rollout, you can finally customize your right-click menu in Windows 11. It fixes 1,094 security flaws, too.

Windows 11 users who’ve struggled to navigate and use the right-click menu in File Explorer now finally have some relief. With the November Patch Tuesday Windows update, you’re now able to customize the menu to add and remove specific commands and apps so that only your favorites appear.

As usual, the monthly update is mandatory, which means it should automatically download and install on your PC. To check, head to Settings and select Windows Update. If the latest update — labeled “2026-11 Security Update (KB5132061) (26300.9974)” -– pops up as installed with a pending restart, just reboot your computer. Otherwise, click the button to check for updates and allow it to download and install.

Also: You can change Windows settings directly from a search now

One caveat: Microsoft’s monthly updates fully support Windows 11 26H2 and 25H2. But support for 24H2 ended last month, at least for the Home and Pro editions. Windows 11 24H2 Enterprise and Education will continue to get monthly security updates, though not regular non-security preview updates, while Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education will receive no more updates after this month.

If you use Windows 11 Home or Pro, be sure you upgrade your system to 26H2 to continue receiving the necessary support and updates.

First and foremost in the latest update is the new customizable right-click menu.

The context-sensitive right-click menu is a handy way to quickly access key settings, features, and apps, both in File Explorer and on the desktop. But there’s always been a flaw in its basic design. The more apps you install, the more cluttered and disorganized the menu becomes. That was especially problematic in previous versions of Windows. The old-style, classic menu would grow so long that it would be difficult to navigate and let you find the item you wanted.

With Windows 11, Microsoft introduced a more modern and pared-down menu. But this version can also get crowded. Plus, it may not display every command you need, so you often have to revert to the older classic menu. You’re then stuck dealing with two separate versions of the same menu, leading to an even more confusing and cumbersome experience.

Also: Windows 11 can run better on PCs with 8GB now, Microsoft says

The ideal solution is a menu that you can customize yourself, and that’s what we now have, at least that’s what is now rolling out. Microsoft calls this one a gradual rollout, which means you may or may not get it right away.

To see if and how this is available, open File Explorer and right-click on a folder or file. If the new menu has reached your PC, you’ll see an entry for Customize menu. Select that to view all the available options for tweaking it. Alternatively, head to Settings, select Personalization, and then click the entry for Context menu.

There, you’re able to turn certain file actions on or off, such as Send to, Print, Create shortcut, Copy as path, and Rotate image. You can also choose which apps appear all the time, either in the main menu or in a submenu. Plus, additional options let you decide where certain commands and actions appear and whether you can still access the old-style menu.

Though the customizable right-click menu is the star of the update, Microsoft has added other surprises as it strives to make Windows more reliable and user-friendly.

Also gradually rolling out, Cloud rebuild is a new recovery option that lets you reinstall Windows 11 via cloud-based system images and drivers downloaded from Windows Update. This tool can help you recover Windows when it won’t load and you don’t have a USB drive or your own custom image. The downside is that your files won’t survive. But if you regularly back them up as you should, you can restore them after Windows is back in business.

To start Cloud rebuild, go to Settings, select System, click Recovery, and then select Rebuild PC. Your PC will then restart into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to kick off the cloud rebuild. If Windows can load, your computer should automatically enter WinRE mode, where you can then choose the cloud rebuild. You should need to make sure your PC is online via a wired or wireless connection.

The November update also enhances or fixes other Windows features and apps.

And that then brings us to the security fixes.

This month’s update resolves 1,094 security vulnerabilities, according to Microsoft, with 63 of them rated critical and one already exploited in the wild. That’s fewer than October’s record of 1,400 patches. But it still represents a hefty number as Microsoft and other vendors continue to rely on AI to find and fix security holes.

Also: Windows finally gets a built-in internet speed test tool – how to try it

The exploited flaw points to a spoofing vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook. Here, a remote attacker who sends you a malicious email and convinces you to open it could cause Outlook to connect to a network controlled by that attacker. In this case, though, you would not receive any warning. Further, the exploit might reveal your username and password to the sender, potentially allowing them to impersonate you.
